title: Cervical Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - the physician decides. Full pathway: presentation/histology -> workup -> FIGO 2018 staging -> stage-directed local therapy (fertility-sparing vs radical surgery vs definitive chemoradiation), each curative arm routed through pathologic-risk or response/restaging decisions before adjuvant therapy or surveillance; locally advanced concurrent cisplatin-radiation +/- pembrolizumab with response-adapted salvage; recurrent disease split by pattern; and metastatic disease as a line-of-therapy sub-tree (first line by PD-L1 CPS -> on progression -> second line -> later line). Small-cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma is a separate platinum-etoposide pathway with response-adapted relapse therapy. Systemic leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id where a dose regimen fits; surgery, radiation, and agents without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Cervical Cancer; no proprietary text reproduced; invents no dose. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Cervical Cancer. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: FIGO 2018 permits imaging and pathologic findings to assign stage; documented nodal involvement raises the stage to IIIC (IIIC1 pelvic, IIIC2 para-aortic). Confirm histology and map local extent before committing to a treatment arm.

b.text: After radical hysterectomy, intermediate-risk features (Sedlis-type: bulky primary, deep stromal invasion, lymphovascular invasion) favor adjuvant pelvic radiation; high-risk features (positive margin, parametrial extension, or positive nodes; Peters-type) favor adjuvant concurrent chemoradiation.

c.text: For higher-risk locally advanced disease (node-positive or bulky), adding pembrolizumab to concurrent cisplatin-radiation and continuing it as maintenance improved outcomes (KEYNOTE-A18 concept). Confirm eligibility and monitor for immune-related toxicity.

d.text: In persistent, recurrent, or metastatic disease, adding pembrolizumab to platinum-doublet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab benefits PD-L1 CPS >= 1 tumors (KEYNOTE-826 concept). Assess PD-L1 CPS by a validated assay before first-line therapy.

e.text: Small-cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix behaves like small-cell carcinoma elsewhere: a platinum + etoposide backbone is prioritized even in localized disease because of the high rate of early distant relapse, and topotecan is a standard option at relapse. Consider brain imaging given the relapse pattern.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Cervical cancer: histology and presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by histology and whether disease is confined to the pelvis or already disseminated. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma (the common histologies) - the main staging pathway
Small-cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma (rare, aggressive - separate systemic-first pathway)
Metastatic (FIGO IVB) or recurrent disease at presentation - systemic pathway

nodes.name: Workup
nodes.title: Workup and staging evaluation
nodes.description: Confirm histology and define local and distant extent before assigning a FIGO stage and treatment arm.
bullets: History and physical with pelvic (and rectovaginal) examination; biopsy-confirmed histology and grade
Pelvic MRI to define tumor size, stromal and parametrial extension
PET-CT (or CT chest/abdomen/pelvis) for nodal and distant disease
Cystoscopy / proctosigmoidoscopy when bladder or rectal invasion is suspected
CBC, renal and liver function, HIV testing; pregnancy status where relevant; fertility counseling if applicable

nodes.name: FIGO stage
nodes.title: FIGO 2018 stage stratification
nodes.description: Assign the FIGO 2018 stage; treatment groups into microinvasive, early operable, locally advanced, and metastatic disease.

tables.title: FIGO 2018 stage groups (simplified) and typical intent
rows: Invasive, confined to cervix / upper vagina, <= 4 cm
Bulky > 4 cm or beyond cervix (parametria, lower vagina, pelvic wall, bladder/rectum)

nodes.name: IA1 LVSI
nodes.title: Stage IA1: lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI)
nodes.description: For IA1, the presence of LVSI escalates local therapy and nodal assessment.

nodes.name: IA1 conservative
nodes.title: Stage IA1 (no LVSI): conization or simple hysterectomy
nodes.description: Microinvasive disease without LVSI is treated conservatively, then surveillance.
bullets: Fertility desired: cervical conization to negative margins; repeat cone if margins involved
Fertility not desired: simple (extrafascial) hysterectomy
No routine pelvic lymph node dissection when LVSI is absent
Then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Fertility wish
nodes.title: Early stage: is fertility preservation desired?
nodes.description: For early operable disease (and IA1 with LVSI), fertility-sparing surgery may be an option for suitable tumors.

nodes.name: Fertility eligibility
nodes.title: Fertility-sparing eligibility
nodes.description: Fertility-sparing surgery is limited to small tumors of favorable histology without high-risk features.
bullets: Generally IA2-IB1 (and selected IB2 up to 2 cm), squamous or usual-type adenocarcinoma
No suspicious nodes, no small-cell / neuroendocrine or gastric-type histology
Nodal assessment (sentinel node / pelvic lymphadenectomy) required first

nodes.name: Fertility-sparing surgery
nodes.title: Fertility-sparing surgery (trachelectomy / cone)
nodes.description: Cervix-preserving resection with nodal staging in eligible early-stage patients; final pathology then guides next steps.
bullets: Radical trachelectomy + pelvic lymph node assessment (IB, up to ~2 cm); cone or simple trachelectomy for very small IA2 tumors
Sentinel lymph node mapping where validated
Adjuvant radiation to a preserved uterus generally precludes future pregnancy - reassess if high-risk pathology is found
Review final pathology before clearing for surveillance and obstetric counseling (next step)

nodes.name: Trachelectomy pathology
nodes.title: Fertility-sparing surgery: final pathology
nodes.description: Final trachelectomy / nodal pathology determines whether fertility preservation holds or definitive adjuvant therapy is required.
bullets: Favorable: negative margins, negative nodes, no high-risk features - fertility preservation stands
Adverse: positive margin / parametria, positive nodes, or unexpected small-cell histology - definitive therapy needed

options.label: Adverse features found (needs adjuvant / definitive therapy)

nodes.name: Surgery vs RT
nodes.title: Early stage: radical surgery vs definitive radiation
nodes.description: Early operable disease can be cured with radical surgery or with definitive radiation; combining both raises morbidity, so choose one primary modality.

nodes.name: Radical hysterectomy
nodes.title: Radical hysterectomy + pelvic lymphadenectomy
nodes.description: Definitive surgery for early operable disease; pathology then guides adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Radical (type B/C) hysterectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection; open approach preferred for oncologic outcome
Sentinel lymph node mapping may supplement full lymphadenectomy in small tumors
Preserve ovaries in premenopausal squamous carcinoma when appropriate
Review surgical pathology for adjuvant risk (next step)

nodes.name: Definitive RT
nodes.title: Definitive radiation for early stage
nodes.description: External-beam radiation plus brachytherapy, with concurrent chemotherapy for higher-risk early tumors; then response is assessed.
bullets: External-beam pelvic radiation + intracavitary brachytherapy to a definitive dose
Add concurrent platinum chemotherapy for bulky or node-positive early tumors
An alternative to surgery with comparable cure rates; avoids combined-modality morbidity
Assess response at restaging before surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early RT response
nodes.title: Definitive RT: response assessment
nodes.description: Restage 3 months after definitive radiation to distinguish a complete response from persistent local disease.
bullets: Examination +/- PET-CT at ~3 months; biopsy any suspicious residual mass
Complete response: enter surveillance
Persistent / progressive local disease: assess for salvage in the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Adjuvant risk
nodes.title: Post-hysterectomy pathologic risk
nodes.description: Adjuvant therapy after radical hysterectomy is directed by pathologic risk features.

options.label: High risk (positive margin, parametria, or nodes)

tables.title: Post-hysterectomy risk features and adjuvant therapy
rows: Positive margin, parametrial extension, or positive pelvic node
Bulky primary + deep stromal invasion + LVSI combinations

nodes.name: Adjuvant chemoRT
nodes.title: Adjuvant concurrent chemoradiation (high risk)
nodes.description: High-risk pathology after surgery is treated with concurrent chemoradiation, then response is assessed.
bullets: Pelvic external-beam radiation with concurrent weekly cisplatin (single-agent radiosensitizer; dose per protocol - no dose asserted here)
Extend the radiation field for para-aortic nodal involvement
Vaginal brachytherapy boost for positive or close vaginal margins
Assess response at restaging (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant response
nodes.title: Adjuvant chemoradiation: response assessment
nodes.description: Restage after adjuvant chemoradiation to confirm disease control or detect early treatment failure.

nodes.name: Adjuvant RT
nodes.title: Adjuvant pelvic radiation (intermediate risk)
nodes.description: Intermediate-risk pathology is treated with adjuvant pelvic radiation to reduce local recurrence, then surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant pelvic external-beam radiation for Sedlis-type intermediate-risk features
Concurrent chemotherapy may be added for higher intermediate-risk combinations
Then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Locally advanced risk
nodes.title: Locally advanced: nodal / risk status
nodes.description: Concurrent chemoradiation is the backbone; adding immunotherapy is considered for higher-risk (node-positive or bulky) disease.

nodes.name: Definitive chemoRT
nodes.title: Definitive concurrent cisplatin-radiation + brachytherapy
nodes.description: Standard curative treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer; response is then assessed.
bullets: External-beam pelvic radiation with concurrent weekly cisplatin as a radiosensitizer (dose per protocol - no dose asserted here)
Image-guided intracavitary +/- interstitial brachytherapy to complete the definitive dose
Extended-field radiation for para-aortic nodal disease (IIIC2)
Complete treatment within an optimal overall time to preserve local control
Assess response at restaging (next step)

nodes.name: ChemoRT + pembrolizumab
nodes.title: Concurrent chemoradiation plus pembrolizumab (higher risk)
nodes.description: For higher-risk locally advanced disease, pembrolizumab is added to concurrent chemoradiation and continued as maintenance; response is then assessed.
bullets: Concurrent cisplatin-radiation + brachytherapy (as above) with pembrolizumab added during and after chemoradiation
Continue pembrolizumab as maintenance per protocol; monitor for immune-related toxicity
Reserve for node-positive or bulky locally advanced disease meeting eligibility
Assess response at restaging (next step)

nodes.name: Locally advanced response
nodes.title: Locally advanced chemoradiation: response assessment
nodes.description: Restage ~3 months after chemoradiation (examination + PET-CT) to separate complete response, persistent local disease, and distant progression - each routes differently.
bullets: Complete metabolic response: enter surveillance
Persistent / residual local disease: consider salvage surgery or boost
Distant progression: move to systemic therapy by PD-L1

nodes.name: Residual-disease salvage
nodes.title: Persistent local disease after chemoradiation: salvage
nodes.description: Biopsy-proven persistent local disease after definitive chemoradiation is treated with salvage local therapy where feasible.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm viable residual tumor before salvage
Salvage hysterectomy or pelvic exenteration for isolated, resectable central residual disease
Brachytherapy / boost if the definitive dose was not completed and tissue tolerance allows
Systemic therapy if unresectable or distant disease emerges; then surveillance if controlled

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy.
bullets: History and physical with speculum / pelvic exam every 3-6 months for 2 years, then 6-12 monthly
Cervical / vaginal cytology as indicated; educate on recurrence symptoms
Imaging (MRI / PET-CT) prompted by symptoms or exam findings, not routinely
Address treatment sequelae: vaginal health, ovarian / sexual function, lymphedema
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence pattern
nodes.title: Recurrent disease: pattern and prior therapy
nodes.description: Salvage intent depends on the site of recurrence and whether the pelvis was previously irradiated.
bullets: Biopsy-confirm recurrence and restage (PET-CT) to define isolated vs disseminated disease

options.label: Central pelvic recurrence after prior radiation

nodes.name: Pelvic exenteration
nodes.title: Central pelvic recurrence: exenteration / salvage surgery
nodes.description: Isolated central recurrence after radiation may be curable with radical salvage surgery.
bullets: Pelvic exenteration for isolated central recurrence after prior full-dose radiation, when no distant disease
Radical hysterectomy may suffice for a small central recurrence in selected cases
Requires fitness assessment and reconstructive / stoma planning
Systemic therapy if unresectable or distant disease is found

nodes.name: Salvage chemoRT
nodes.title: Radiation-naive pelvic recurrence: salvage chemoradiation
nodes.description: A pelvic recurrence in a previously non-irradiated field can be treated with curative-intent chemoradiation.
bullets: Concurrent cisplatin-radiation + brachytherapy to the recurrence (dose per protocol - no dose asserted here)
Consider surgical resection first if isolated and resectable
Then surveillance or systemic therapy per response

nodes.name: Oligometastatic
nodes.title: Oligometastatic recurrence: local ablation + systemic
nodes.description: Limited metastatic sites may be treated with local ablative therapy alongside systemic therapy directed by PD-L1.
bullets: Stereotactic body radiation or metastasectomy to limited sites (e.g. isolated lung / node)
Add first-line systemic therapy directed by PD-L1 (next step)
Reassess for disseminated progression at follow-up

nodes.name: PD-L1 (metastatic)
nodes.title: Metastatic / recurrent: PD-L1 (CPS) stratification
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for persistent, recurrent, or metastatic disease is directed by PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS).

tables.title: PD-L1 CPS and first-line systemic backbone

nodes.name: Pembro + chemo + bev
nodes.title: First-line (PD-L1 CPS >= 1): pembrolizumab + chemo + bevacizumab
nodes.description: Add pembrolizumab to a platinum-doublet plus bevacizumab for PD-L1-positive metastatic / recurrent disease; on progression, move to second line.
bullets: Carboplatin (or cisplatin) + paclitaxel + bevacizumab, with pembrolizumab added and continued as maintenance
Confirm no bevacizumab contraindication (fistula, uncontrolled hypertension, recent bleeding)
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
Chemotherapy + bevacizumab backbone referenced below (pembrolizumab added on top - no dose asserted here)
On progression, proceed to second-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Chemo + bev
nodes.title: First-line (PD-L1 CPS < 1): chemotherapy + bevacizumab
nodes.description: Platinum-doublet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab for PD-L1-negative metastatic / recurrent disease; on progression, move to second line.
bullets: Carboplatin (or cisplatin) + paclitaxel + bevacizumab
Cisplatin-paclitaxel-bevacizumab is an alternative doublet backbone
Confirm no bevacizumab contraindication
Regimen referenced below
On progression, proceed to second-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Second line
nodes.title: Metastatic: second-line therapy (on progression)
nodes.description: After progression on first-line therapy, second-line options are directed by biomarkers and prior immunotherapy exposure.

nodes.name: Second-line IO
nodes.title: Second-line immunotherapy
nodes.description: Immunotherapy for biomarker-selected or immunotherapy-naive recurrent disease; on progression, later-line options apply.
bullets: Pembrolizumab for dMMR/MSI-high or TMB-high tumors (tissue-agnostic), if immunotherapy-naive
Single-agent anti-PD-1 for PD-L1-positive disease not previously treated with immunotherapy
Consider NTRK-fusion targeted therapy if an actionable fusion is present
No dose asserted here - agent regimen per protocol
On progression, proceed to later-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Tisotumab vedotin
nodes.title: Second-line antibody-drug conjugate (tisotumab vedotin)
nodes.description: Tissue-factor-directed antibody-drug conjugate after progression on first-line therapy; on progression, later-line options apply.
bullets: Tisotumab vedotin (tissue-factor-directed ADC) after prior systemic therapy
Monitor ocular toxicity (prophylactic eye care), bleeding, and peripheral neuropathy
No dose asserted here - agent regimen per protocol
On progression, proceed to later-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Later line
nodes.title: Metastatic: later-line therapy (on further progression)
nodes.description: After progression on second-line therapy, options are single-agent chemotherapy, a clinical trial, or supportive care by performance status and goals.

nodes.name: Later-line chemo
nodes.title: Later-line single-agent chemotherapy
nodes.description: Sequential single-agent chemotherapy for platinum-resistant recurrent / metastatic disease.
bullets: Options: topotecan, gemcitabine, vinorelbine, pemetrexed, or a taxane not previously used
Platinum re-challenge for a long platinum-free interval
Modest response rates; weigh toxicity against performance status and goals of care
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Clinical trial
nodes.title: Clinical trial enrollment
nodes.description: Enrollment in a clinical trial is encouraged for heavily pretreated recurrent / metastatic disease.
bullets: Prioritize trials of novel ADCs, bispecifics, or targeted agents matched to molecular profiling
Broad molecular profiling (NGS) to identify actionable alterations
Maintain supportive care in parallel

nodes.name: Supportive care
nodes.title: Best supportive / palliative care
nodes.description: Symptom-directed palliative care when disease-directed therapy is not appropriate or desired.
bullets: Palliative radiation for bleeding, pain, or obstructive symptoms
Manage pain, fistula, renal obstruction (nephrostomy / stent), and psychosocial needs
Early palliative-care and goals-of-care discussion

nodes.name: Neuroendocrine extent
nodes.title: Small-cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma: disease extent
nodes.description: This aggressive histology is treated with early systemic chemotherapy integrated with local therapy; extent determines whether local therapy is combined with chemotherapy or chemotherapy is given alone.

nodes.name: Neuroendocrine limited
nodes.title: Neuroendocrine (limited): chemotherapy + local therapy
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide chemotherapy integrated with concurrent chemoradiation or surgery for pelvis-confined small-cell / neuroendocrine disease; response is then assessed.
bullets: Platinum + etoposide chemotherapy is the systemic backbone (small-cell pattern)
Combine with concurrent chemoradiation for local control, or surgery + adjuvant chemotherapy in early operable cases
Systemic therapy is prioritized even in localized disease given the high rate of early distant relapse
Backbone referenced below; assess response at restaging (next step)

nodes.name: Neuroendocrine extensive
nodes.title: Neuroendocrine (extensive): systemic chemotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide systemic chemotherapy for extensive / metastatic small-cell / neuroendocrine disease; response is then assessed.
bullets: Platinum + etoposide systemic chemotherapy (small-cell pattern)
Palliative radiation to symptomatic sites as needed
Consider brain imaging given the relapse pattern
Backbone referenced below; assess response at restaging (next step)

nodes.name: Neuroendocrine response
nodes.title: Neuroendocrine: response assessment
nodes.description: Restage after platinum-etoposide chemotherapy to guide surveillance or relapse therapy.

nodes.name: Neuroendocrine relapse
nodes.title: Neuroendocrine relapse: second-line chemotherapy
nodes.description: Relapsed small-cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma is treated with second-line chemotherapy by platinum-free interval.
bullets: Topotecan is a standard second-line option (small-cell pattern)
Platinum-etoposide re-challenge for a long platinum-free interval; consider a clinical trial
Supportive / palliative care in parallel by performance status
Second-line regimen referenced below
